entity_resolution.arabic_name: أبو علي، الحسن بن الحسن بن الهيثم

timeline_a_biological.event: Born in Basra during the Buwayhid dynasty.
Moved to Cairo under the Fatimid Caliphate; feigned madness to escape Caliph al-Hakim's punishment after assessing the Nile damming project as unfeasible.
Released from house arrest following the death of Caliph al-Hakim.
Died in Cairo at approximately age 75.

timeline_b_scientific.description: Began drafting 'Kitab al-Manazir' (Book of Optics) during decade-long house arrest.
Completed 'Kitab al-Manazir', establishing experimental optics and proving the intromission theory of vision.
Formulated Alhazen's Problem in catoptrics regarding light reflection off spherical surfaces.
Authored 'Maqala fi al-Daw' (Treatise on Light) demonstrating camera obscura and linear propagation of light rays.

physics_analysis.contribution_name: Intromission Theory of Vision and Camera Obscura Optics
physics_analysis.scientific_problem: Determining whether vision occurs via rays emitted from the eye (extramission) or rays entering the eye from luminous sources (intromission).
physics_analysis.hypothesis: Light rays travel in straight lines from light-emitting or light-reflecting points on an object and enter the eye to form an image geometrically.
physics_analysis.model_or_framework: Geometric Ray Optics and Experimental Camera Obscura Model.
physics_analysis.experiment_details: Utilized a darkened chamber (al-Bayt al-Muthlim) with a small aperture (pinhole) to project images of outdoor lanterns onto a screen, showing inversion and linear propagation.

equations.validity_domain: Geometric optics approximation where aperture diameter is significantly smaller than object distance, but large enough to ignore diffraction limits.
equations.assumptions: Light travels in strictly straight lines through uniform media without diffraction.

physics_analysis.result_and_impact: Disproved Ptolemaic and Euclidean extramission theories, laid the foundation for modern optics, and formalized the controlled empirical scientific method.
physics_analysis.limitations_and_boundary_conditions: Did not account for wave phenomena such as diffraction or refraction dynamics at micro-scales.

physics_analysis.scientific_problem: Finding the point on a spherical mirror where a ray from a fixed light source reflects to an observer's eye.
physics_analysis.hypothesis: The point of reflection on a spherical surface can be solved geometrically via the intersection of a circle and a hyperbola, conforming to equal incident and reflected angles.
physics_analysis.model_or_framework: Non-linear geometric catoptrics using conic sections.
physics_analysis.experiment_details: Constructed specialized brass spherical, parabolic, and cylindrical mirrors to empirically verify reflection angles against theoretical conic intersection points.

equations.latex_raw: x^4 + a x^3 + b x^2 + c x + d = 0

variables_definition.x: Coordinate of the reflection point on the mirror surface
variables_definition.a, b, c, d: Geometric constants derived from source location, observer location, and mirror radius

equations.validity_domain: Reflection off specular spherical surfaces in Euclidean 2D/3D space.
equations.assumptions: Smooth, ideal spherical reflecting surface governed by equal angle law (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection).

physics_analysis.result_and_impact: Spurred development of geometric and analytic methods in Europe; solved algebraically centuries later by Christiaan Huygens.
physics_analysis.limitations_and_boundary_conditions: Required geometric conic construction; lacked modern algebraic notation for analytic reduction.
